{"id":"ENG-2165","uuid":"8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea","title":"Refactor Roam Sync to use crossAppNodes","description":"## Problem

* We have two paths to write to the database: sync and publish. They use different converters, which violates DRY.
  * Sync converts with `discourseNodeSchemaToLocalConcept`, `discourseNodeBlockToLocalConcept`, `convertRoamNodeToLocalContent` and `convertRoamNodeToFullContent`. It writes with `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content` (`syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts`).
  * Publish converts with `crossAppNodeToDbConcept` and writes with `upsert_concepts` (`publishNodesToGroups.ts`).
* We want the sync to use the same CrossApp converters as publish.

## Solution

* Large-scale: Rewrite the sync to use the publish converters.
  * To be broken down in sub-tasks
* PR <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> is not code I think we should check in as-is, but Claude-generated code which I sent to help us understand the scope and surface.

**Open decisions**

1. Is this ticket a step of <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>, or does it replace <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>?
   * As a step, this ticket moves sync onto the Roam-to-CrossApp converters and keeps the current write calls. <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue> then makes the single write.
   * This answers <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>'s Open decision 2.
2. Which smaller tickets does <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> split into, and in what order? Michael asked for the split on 2026-08-28.
3. Do the items <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> deferred get their own tickets? They are `nodeTypeSince` missing child-block edits, and published isFirstChild nodes needing both a `direct_and_description` and a `direct` Content.

## Done When

* The old sync path using RoamFullContentNode is removed.
  * This will include <issue id="17320a42-9f07-49ff-bc23-ba9586e335bf" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2061/refactor-roamfullcontentnode-to-use-crossappnode-contract">ENG-2061</issue>
* The sync path only upserts Concepts, with embedded Content, vs the two phases we have now.
  * <issue id="b2336c31-b4ea-4e9a-886f-cf8e81c55e6a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1794/atomic-upsert-of-concept-and-content">ENG-1794</issue>
  * <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue> has the same Done When. Open decision 1 decides which ticket owns it.

## Out of Scope

* Moving Roam publish to the upsert route. <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>'s Open decision 3 covers it.

## Notes

* Current state:
  * PR <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> is a draft. It conflicts with main and was last updated on 2026-08-23.
  * If the upsert route stays the goal (<issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue>), sync only converts Roam data to CrossApp types, and the route converts them to database rows.
  * The sync schema converter now writes `template_content` (`conceptConversion.ts`), so the "template key" problem in the investigation below looks fixed on main.
* We still need to handle the discrepancy between direct and direct_and_description
  * Separate task but describing here
  * Published nodes with isFirst child need both to be maintained by sync
    * In sync, we can put the direct_and_description variant in the direct field of the Content (for isFirstChild nodes)
    * And send the direct variant of published, isFirstChild nodes at sync, as a separate content upsert.
  * Nodes without isFirstChild need only direct, so that is what sync will send.

{"id":"ENG-2061","uuid":"17320a42-9f07-49ff-bc23-ba9586e335bf","title":"Refactor `RoamFullContentNode` to use `CrossAppNode` contract","description":"## Problem

* `RoamFullContentNode` and `CrossAppNode` describe the same node. Michael: "It is basically the same type, different name" ([type](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1243/changes#diff-740e5638ca02078f61f320b8654a1a5b2cad3350046a466abd1f8bf556c95b95L11>)).
  * `RoamFullContentNode` (`convertRoamNodeToFullContent.ts`) is a flat datalog row: snake_case fields, times typed `string | number`, and `text`, `format` and `node_title`.
  * `CrossAppNode` is nested, with `content.direct` and `content.full`.
* Michael: "This likely removes the need for this converter" ([converter](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1243/changes#diff-3369b2954fe17df153f37f163d9fb033a7afd3063bf9e77142aed5ff214e805aR5>)). The converter, `fullContentNodeToCrossApp` (`roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`), derives `coreTitle` from the title format and builds the full content. That work moves; it doesn't go away.

## Solution

* Remove `RoamFullContentNode`. <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>'s Done When includes this ticket.

{"id":"ENG-1824","uuid":"dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f","title":"Use the unified upsert_concepts in Roam","description":"## Problem

* Roam sync writes Concepts and Content in separate calls, to `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content`. If one call fails, we have partially defined nodes in the database.
* It would be better to send the full node, with Content as sub-objects of the Concept, in a single upsert. `upsert_concepts` accepts this since <issue id="b66b4d29-6edc-4fbe-bbbc-4cfaab6f9834" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1822/modify-upsert-concepts-so-it-accepts-embedded-content">ENG-1822</issue>.
* Roam publish already writes in a single call. Roam sync does not.

## Solution

* Remove the calls to `upsert_content`. Unify the Content computations to create the CrossAppNode type, and send it, after conversion, in a single call.

**Open decisions**

1. Does the single call go through the upsert route (<issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue>) or straight to `upsert_concepts`? On 2026-07-17 we agreed on the route. <issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue> has to confirm that still holds after v0.
2. <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue> (Roam sync onto the CrossApp converters) is the same work. Is it a step of this ticket, or does it replace this ticket? <issue id="b90793f4-5dc0-40fc-9942-95895531ba24" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2413/decide-how-roam-and-obsidian-move-onto-the-crossapp-types">ENG-2413</issue> decides this.
3. If we use the route, does this ticket also move Roam publish to it? Publish calls `upsert_concepts` directly today, and no ticket covers moving it.

## Done When

* There is no `upsert_content` call left in the Roam codebase, including test harnesses.

## Out of Scope

## Notes

* Today's `upsert_content` calls: `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts` (two calls) and `upsertNodesAsContentWithEmbeddings.ts`. Test harnesses: `fileReferenceHarness.ts` and `syncSharedNodeAssets.test.ts`.

{"id":"ENG-1824","uuid":"dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f","title":"Use the unified upsert_concepts in Roam","description":"## Problem

* Roam sync writes Concepts and Content in separate calls, to `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content`. If one call fails, we have partially defined nodes in the database.
* It would be better to send the full node, with Content as sub-objects of the Concept, in a single upsert. `upsert_concepts` accepts this since <issue id="b66b4d29-6edc-4fbe-bbbc-4cfaab6f9834" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1822/modify-upsert-concepts-so-it-accepts-embedded-content">ENG-1822</issue>.
* Roam publish already writes in a single call. Roam sync does not.

## Solution

* Remove the calls to `upsert_content`. Unify the Content computations to create the CrossAppNode type, and send it, after conversion, in a single call.

**Open decisions**

1. Does the single call go through the upsert route (<issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue>) or straight to `upsert_concepts`? On 2026-07-17 we agreed on the route. <issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue> has to confirm that still holds after v0.
2. <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue> (Roam sync onto the CrossApp converters) is the same work. Is it a step of this ticket, or does it replace this ticket? <issue id="b90793f4-5dc0-40fc-9942-95895531ba24" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2413/decide-how-roam-and-obsidian-move-onto-the-crossapp-types">ENG-2413</issue> decides this.
3. If we use the route, does this ticket also move Roam publish to it? Publish calls `upsert_concepts` directly today, and no ticket covers moving it.

## Done When

* There is no `upsert_content` call left in the Roam codebase, including test harnesses.

## Out of Scope

## Notes

* Today's `upsert_content` calls: `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts` (two calls) and `upsertNodesAsContentWithEmbeddings.ts`. Test harnesses: `fileReferenceHarness.ts` and `syncSharedNodeAssets.test.ts`.

{"id":"ENG-2165","uuid":"8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea","title":"Refactor Roam Sync to use crossAppNodes","description":"## Problem

* We have two paths to write to the database: sync and publish. They use different converters, which violates DRY.
  * Sync converts with `discourseNodeSchemaToLocalConcept`, `discourseNodeBlockToLocalConcept`, `convertRoamNodeToLocalContent` and `convertRoamNodeToFullContent`. It writes with `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content` (`syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts`).
  * Publish converts with `crossAppNodeToDbConcept` and writes with `upsert_concepts` (`publishNodesToGroups.ts`).
* We want the sync to use the same CrossApp converters as publish.

## Solution

* Large-scale: Rewrite the sync to use the publish converters.
  * To be broken down in sub-tasks
* PR <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> is not code I think we should check in as-is, but Claude-generated code which I sent to help us understand the scope and surface.

**Open decisions**

1. Is this ticket a step of <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>, or does it replace <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>?
   * As a step, this ticket moves sync onto the Roam-to-CrossApp converters and keeps the current write calls. <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue> then makes the single write.
   * This answers <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>'s Open decision 2.
2. Which smaller tickets does <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> split into, and in what order? Michael asked for the split on 2026-08-28.
3. Do the items <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> deferred get their own tickets? They are `nodeTypeSince` missing child-block edits, and published isFirstChild nodes needing both a `direct_and_description` and a `direct` Content.

## Done When

* The old sync path using RoamFullContentNode is removed.
  * This will include <issue id="17320a42-9f07-49ff-bc23-ba9586e335bf" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2061/refactor-roamfullcontentnode-to-use-crossappnode-contract">ENG-2061</issue>
* The sync path only upserts Concepts, with embedded Content, vs the two phases we have now.
  * <issue id="b2336c31-b4ea-4e9a-886f-cf8e81c55e6a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1794/atomic-upsert-of-concept-and-content">ENG-1794</issue>
  * <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue> has the same Done When. Open decision 1 decides which ticket owns it.

## Out of Scope

* Moving Roam publish to the upsert route. <issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>'s Open decision 3 covers it.

## Notes

* Current state:
  * PR <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> is a draft. It conflicts with main and was last updated on 2026-08-23.
  * If the upsert route stays the goal (<issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue>), sync only converts Roam data to CrossApp types, and the route converts them to database rows.
  * The sync schema converter now writes `template_content` (`conceptConversion.ts`), so the "template key" problem in the investigation below looks fixed on main.
* We still need to handle the discrepancy between direct and direct_and_description
  * Separate task but describing here
  * Published nodes with isFirst child need both to be maintained by sync
    * In sync, we can put the direct_and_description variant in the direct field of the Content (for isFirstChild nodes)
    * And send the direct variant of published, isFirstChild nodes at sync, as a separate content upsert.
  * Nodes without isFirstChild need only direct, so that is what sync will send.
* I had Claude do this, thinking it appropriate while working on <issue id="2565264d-8db7-4380-97b8-aad006e7e143" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2128/express-source-as-a-sourcedocument-slotreference-of-evidence">ENG-2128</issue>. It was decided that the testing would take too long, so it will be delayed. Still thinking it's worth examining the choices made while writing that code.
* Here are some decision points identified by Claude while doing this. Items marked "your design", "your call" or "you accepted" are Marc-Antoine's decisions; the others are Claude's choices.
  * Investigation — why schema updates never landed
    * Two independent sync paths, disagreeing: publishNodesToGroups used the cross-app converters but only inserted schemas missing from my_concepts; syncDgNodesToSupabase re-upserted schemas but through converters that emitted no slots and put template content under the template key that Obsidian reads as a template name.
    * The server was never the constraint — upsert_concepts already does ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE. Both gaps were client-side.
    * nodeTypeSince misses child-block edits (it tests :edit/time on the type block, while format lives in a child). Still unfixed; it means schema changes reach the DB mainly via sharedNodeTypeIds.

    sync-should-use-CrossApp
    * Concept names preserved for block-backed nodes ("{page title} {block text}") — otherwise every such concept would be renamed against a unique (space_id, name) index.
    * Variant became a property of the content, not of the slot it sits in — your design. That let the direct slot host a direct_and_description.
    * Missing first child → plain direct — your call.
    * The two-phase sync collapsed into one — your call, and it retired the withContents flag I'd added as a workaround. You read that flag correctly as a symptom.
    * Embeddings only for changed nodes — a node present solely for a full-content backfill hasn't changed and keeps its own.
    * CONCEPT_BATCH_SIZE 200 → 50, since concepts now carry full page markdown.
    * slot → defaultVariant — my rename collided with Concept.slots.
    * RoamFullContentNode removed, and times declared number (option A) rather than widened to string | number — number is both narrower and true, since all three producers are datalog rows.
    * Telemetry attribution shifts — markdown building moved into the getSharedFullContentUpdates phase; you accepted that.

    Deferred, deliberately
    * nodeTypeSince's blindness to child-block edits.
    * A published isFirstChild node sending both a direct_and_description and a plain direct (recorded as a comment in roamToCrossAppConverters.ts).
    * Producers returning CrossAppNode directly, together with folding node-type content into schema concepts — they share the upsertNodeSchemaToContent seam.
* History:
  * 2026-07-15 meeting: Michael wrote that callers move to the CrossApp contracts only "until such time as the linear task says to update the caller to use `CrossApp` contract". [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/7iirRHpUd>)
  * 2026-07-22 meeting: Michael: "keep all roam to cross app converters in a single file". [Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/Ic0cf7vkT>)
  * 2026-08-04 meeting: Michael wrote that client functions convert "from roam/obsidian data > CrossApp\* contracts", and "this is BEFORE the post-converter eg CrossApp\* > Database". {"id":"ENG-2061","uuid":"17320a42-9f07-49ff-bc23-ba9586e335bf","title":"Refactor `RoamFullContentNode` to use `CrossAppNode` contract","description":"## Problem

* `RoamFullContentNode` and `CrossAppNode` describe the same node. Michael: "It is basically the same type, different name" ([type](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1243/changes#diff-740e5638ca02078f61f320b8654a1a5b2cad3350046a466abd1f8bf556c95b95L11>)).
  * `RoamFullContentNode` (`convertRoamNodeToFullContent.ts`) is a flat datalog row: snake_case fields, times typed `string | number`, and `text`, `format` and `node_title`.
  * `CrossAppNode` is nested, with `content.direct` and `content.full`.
* Michael: "This likely removes the need for this converter" ([converter](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1243/changes#diff-3369b2954fe17df153f37f163d9fb033a7afd3063bf9e77142aed5ff214e805aR5>)). The converter, `fullContentNodeToCrossApp` (`roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`), derives `coreTitle` from the title format and builds the full content. That work moves; it doesn't go away.

## Solution

* Remove `RoamFullContentNode`. <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>'s Done When includes this ticket.

**Open decisions**

1. Is this the first sub-ticket of <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>, part of <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue>'s single change, or closed because `RoamFullContentNode` is a fair input row type?
2. Does the full-content producer, `getSharedRoamNodesWithFullContentUpdatesSince`, return `CrossAppNode` directly? <pull-request id="8bb57b65-2115-4953-b1b7-b124ccef369c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2165-refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes-70d99b932447">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1333</pull-request> removed the type but deferred "Producers returning CrossAppNode directly".
3. Does this ticket also cover `RoamDiscourseNodeData` (`getAllDiscourseNodesSince.ts`), the row type the direct-content path uses? No ticket covers it.

## Done When

* `RoamFullContentNode` is gone from the Roam codebase, including tests.

## Out of Scope

* Changing the sync write calls (<issue id="dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824/use-the-unified-upsert-concepts-in-roam">ENG-1824</issue>).

{"id":"ENG-1824","uuid":"dee6db2f-6461-4f53-9c6b-8a015921099f","title":"Use the unified upsert_concepts in Roam","description":"## Problem

* Roam sync writes Concepts and Content in separate calls, to `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content`. If one call fails, we have partially defined nodes in the database.
* It would be better to send the full node, with Content as sub-objects of the Concept, in a single upsert. `upsert_concepts` accepts this since <issue id="b66b4d29-6edc-4fbe-bbbc-4cfaab6f9834" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1822/modify-upsert-concepts-so-it-accepts-embedded-content">ENG-1822</issue>.
* Roam publish already writes in a single call. Roam sync does not.

## Solution

* Remove the calls to `upsert_content`. Unify the Content computations to create the CrossAppNode type, and send it, after conversion, in a single call.

**Open decisions**

1. Does the single call go through the upsert route (<issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue>) or straight to `upsert_concepts`? On 2026-07-17 we agreed on the route. <issue id="eeed8918-ccd5-4056-a629-c09660968d99" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890/create-a-generic-upsert-route-that-accepts-all-root-crossapp-types">FEE-890</issue> has to confirm that still holds after v0.
2. <issue id="8f04a7a2-c757-47d2-b12f-c918a32b77ea" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165/refactor-roam-sync-to-use-crossappnodes">ENG-2165</issue> (Roam sync onto the CrossApp converters) is the same work. Is it a step of this ticket, or does it replace this ticket? <issue id="b90793f4-5dc0-40fc-9942-95895531ba24" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2413/decide-how-roam-and-obsidian-move-onto-the-crossapp-types">ENG-2413</issue> decides this.
3. If we use the route, does this ticket also move Roam publish to it? Publish calls `upsert_concepts` directly today, and no ticket covers moving it.

## Done When

* There is no `upsert_content` call left in the Roam codebase, including test harnesses.

## Out of Scope

## Notes

* Today's `upsert_content` calls: `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts` (two calls) and `upsertNodesAsContentWithEmbeddings.ts`. Test harnesses: `fileReferenceHarness.ts` and `syncSharedNodeAssets.test.ts`.
* History:
  * 2026-05-30: Marc-Antoine created this as the Roam half of <issue id="b2336c31-b4ea-4e9a-886f-cf8e81c55e6a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1794/atomic-upsert-of-concept-and-content">ENG-1794</issue>.
  * 2026-06-25: Marc-Antoine: "Best done after <issue id="585c1ffc-4a96-443d-81a7-ced2414a7b58" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-892/add-roam-full-markdown-content-variant-for-shared-nodes">ENG-1848</issue>" (now <issue id="585c1ffc-4a96-443d-81a7-ced2414a7b58" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-892/add-roam-full-markdown-content-variant-for-shared-nodes">FEE-892</issue>).

content.thinking:
I'm trying to reconcile PR #1333's approach of having fullContentNodeToCrossApp take RoamDiscourseNodeData with the stated decision that the full-content query should return CrossAppNode directly rather than as a separate step, so I need to check how getSharedRoamNodesWithFullContentUpdatesSince actually builds things.

PR #1333 also deleted convertRoamNodeToFullContent.ts and made fullContentNodeToCrossApp consume RoamDiscourseNodeData instead, with its time fields now numeric and author_name optional, while the producer builds the CrossAppNode at the end using that converter. So the "RoamDiscourseNodeData as a later step" answer really means don't touch or refactor that row type further beyond what #1333 already changed — it's out of scope for this ticket.

But now main has added a `format` field to RoamFullContentNode (needed for coreTitle), which RoamDiscourseNodeData doesn't carry, so I need to figure out how fullContentNodeToCrossApp would get access to format if it's meant to take RoamDiscourseNodeData as input — maybe the producer passes format as a separate argument alongside the row.

I'm also reconsidering whether the producer should return CrossAppNode directly rather than RoamFullContentNode — that's what PR #1333 actually did, wrapping the node with a nodeTypeId, which seems to align with what ENG-2165 is asking for around folding node-type content into schema concepts.

PR #1333 says the decision isn't part of it, which leaves me unsure whether "returning CrossAppNode directly" means skipping the intermediate RoamDiscourseNodeData literal before mapping to CrossAppNode — it's genuinely ambiguous, so I need to figure out the minimal, sensible scope of that removal.

Following the #1333 pattern consistently, I'd delete convertRoamNodeToFullContent.ts entirely (including the RoamFullContentNode and ConvertedFullContent types), have fullContentNodeToCrossApp take RoamDiscourseNodeData plus format, and have the producer build the CrossAppNode through that helper. Then upsertSharedNodesFullContentWithAssets would accept CrossAppNode[] and run crossAppNodeToDbContent, though I'm still working out how to handle the error cases that the original try/catch around buildFullInlineContent was catching.

If I move markdown building into the producer, the try/catch has to move too, which shifts telemetry attribution — and there's a comment on main added after #1333 explicitly saying markdown building stays inside the "upsertFullContent" phase since it's the expensive half of the upload and timing depends on that placement. So I need an alternative where the producer just returns the raw rows and format, letting upsertSharedNodesFullContentWithAssets keep doing the markdown build internally to preserve that timing boundary.

That actually matches the decision I found — the full-content query is NOT supposed to return CrossAppNode directly, it should keep returning the existing row type, with conversion happening inside the phase where it already lives. That keeps telemetry intact and the diff minimal, so my plan for ENG-2061 is to change the input type that fullContentNodeToCrossApp expects to the new row shape while leaving everything else where it is.

I'm interpreting the decision's mention of RoamDiscourseNodeData as tied to Open decision 3, about whether this ticket also removes/retypes that row type. On PR #1216 (ENG-2019), relocating Obsidian's `metadata as Record<string, any>` casts made CI's eslint check annotate the "pre-existing" `no-explicit-any` warnings on the new lines. sid flagged them ("these types of eslint errors").

**Why:** The GitHub eslint annotator attributes warnings to whoever last touched the line. "Warning-neutral relocation" is not neutral on the PR — the reviewer sees new warnings.

**How to apply:** When a swap/extraction moves lines that carry lint warnings, fix the underlying issue in the same PR instead of preserving the pattern. For `Json` metadata access: narrow with `x !== null && typeof x === "object" && !Array.isArray(x)` — TS then resolves property access natively, no casts. Check `npx eslint` on touched files against the OLD count and expect it to go down, not stay equal.

**The exact CI mechanism** (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`, `lint-changed-files`, verified 2026-07-27): eslint runs on whole changed *files*, but the result goes through `reviewdog -filter-mode=added -fail-level=warning`. So warnings on lines the diff does NOT touch never fail the job — only added/changed lines do. Practical consequence: adding a one-token edit to a file full of pre-existing warnings is safe, and `npx eslint --max-warnings 0 <file>` failing locally is not by itself a CI failure. Confirm which lines the warnings sit on (`diff` your change against `origin/main`) before spending effort on unrelated ones.

# Style Guide

This document outlines the coding standards and best practices for contributing to Discourse Graphs.

## TypeScript Guidelines

- Prefer `type` over `interface`
- Use explicit return types for functions
- Avoid `any` types when possible
- Prefer arrow functions over regular function declarations
- Use named parameters (object destructuring) when a function has more than 2 parameters

## UI Guidelines

- Use [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) for styling where possible
- When refactoring inline styles, use Tailwind classes.
- Use platform-native UI components first ([blueprintjs for Roam](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/developer-documentation/page/5BB8h4I7b), [Lucide icons for Obsidian](https://help.obsidian.md/Contributing+to+Obsidian/Style+guide), etc), with [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) as a fallback
- Maintain visual consistency with the host application's design system
- Follow responsive design principles
- Use `text-red-700` for Roam error message text. Obsidian keeps `text-error`; website and shared UI keep `text-destructive`. This convention does not change danger buttons, borders, backgrounds, or diagram colors.

## Code Formatting

- Use Prettier with the project's configuration
- Maintain consistent naming conventions:
  - PascalCase for components and types
  - camelCase for variables and functions
  - UPPERCASE for constants

## Code comments

Ask: **What would a maintainer get wrong if this comment were removed?** If there is no specific answer, remove it.

Keep comments that explain non-obvious decisions, external API or data constraints, known limitations, side effects, or ordering requirements. Prefer descriptive names when they can convey the same information.

Before keeping a comment, check:

- **Necessary:** Would removing it hide information needed to safely change or use the code?
- **Accurate:** Does it match what the code actually does, including relevant limitations and exceptions?
- **Concise:** Can it be shortened without losing necessary information?
- **Durable:** Will it still matter after this PR merges?
- **Local:** Is it next to the code that depends on the information?

Prefer one or two short sentences. Use longer explanations or examples when the constraint requires them; this is not a hard length limit.

Do not restate function names, types, test names, assertions, or obvious operations. Do not repeat an explanation already documented at its source; link to it when needed.

Put implementation history, review iterations, scope justifications, and ticket splits in inline GitHub comments. Keep durable constraints and known limitations in code or linked documentation. Link to the decision when describing behavior as agreed or accepted.

Agents must check added and modified comments against these criteria before handoff. Authors must review them manually before requesting review.

## Code Organization

- Prefer small, focused functions over inline code
- Co-locate code with its primary usage. Export it only for a concrete reuse need.
- Move code to `/utils` when it is shared across multiple call sites. Consider a shared package only after the code has stabilized and proven broadly reusable.
- Ground code movement in a current use case. Moving code because it feels cleaner adds churn without a clear functional benefit.
- Extract complex logic into well-named functions
- Prefer early returns over nested conditionals for better readability
- Function names should describe their purpose clearly:

```typescript
// ❌ Unclear and inline
const result = items.filter(
  (x) => x.date > now && x.status === "active" && !x.isArchived,
);

// ✅ Clear and reusable
const getActiveUnarchivedItems = (items: Item[]) => {
  return items.filter(isActiveAndUnarchived);
};

const isActiveAndUnarchived = (item: Item) => {
  return item.date > now && item.status === "active" && !item.isArchived;
};
```

- Choose descriptive function names that make comments unnecessary:

```typescript
  // ❌ Needs a comment to explain
  // Check if user can access premium features
  const check = (user: User) => { ... }

  // ✅ Self-documenting function name
  const hasValidPremiumSubscription = (user: User) => { ... }
```

- Break down complex operations into smaller, meaningful functions:

```typescript
// ❌ Large, multi-purpose function
const processData = (data: Data) => {
  // 30 lines of validation
  // 20 lines of transformation
  // 15 lines of formatting
};

// ✅ Composed of focused functions
const processData = (data: Data) => {
  const validatedData = validateDataFormat(data);
  const transformedData = transformToDesiredFormat(validatedData);
  return formatForDisplay(transformedData);
};
```

## Documentation

- Use sentence case by default in docs and UI copy. Capitalize official product/plugin names and exact UI labels, buttons, or page titles, but keep generic feature terms lowercase.

## Code hygiene

- Remove unused imports, temporary comments, and debug logging before requesting review. Preserve intentional operational logging.
- Handle errors gracefully and log enough context to diagnose failures without exposing credentials or sensitive data.

## Testing

- Write unit tests for new functionality
- Ensure tests are meaningful and maintainable
- Cover relevant edge cases, error paths, and alternative flows.
- Expose workspace unit tests through a `test:unit` script so the root validation command includes them.
# PR guidelines

This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.

## Size and review guidance

About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.

Test changes do not count toward the 400-line threshold.

Above 400 changed lines, explain why the PR cannot reasonably be split. Include the main review entry points and intended testing path in Reviewer brief. Keep this concise rather than adding a file-by-file summary.

## Branches and PR metadata

- Use Linear's generated branch name through Copy Branch Name.
- For Linear-backed work, use `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` as the PR title. This is the repository convention in place of the alternative title formats previously listed in DevOps.
- Start with [.github/pull_request_template.md](.github/pull_request_template.md). Treat the ticket as the source of truth rather than restating it. Follow the PR body guidance in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#pull-request-bodies).

## Before requesting review

- Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root before opening a PR or declaring it ready. Resolve failures before requesting review. A draft must disclose unresolved validation blockers.
- Check applicable build and lint commands. Manually exercise changed behavior end-to-end, including relevant edge cases and alternative flows. Verification is optional; use it when checks and results help the reviewer.
- Read the complete final diff and review it against [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md), including added and modified comments. Use inline PR comments for review-specific explanations and durable code comments for constraints future changes must preserve.
- Run `$scope-check` against the ENG ticket and final diff. Paste its Scope check section into the PR body. If `Done When` is missing, leave the checkbox unchecked and state that explicitly.
- Run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata. Check the Standards check box when it has run. Make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them.
- Complete the Local delegated full review required by the template, using `$dg-delegated-full-review` when no other full-review workflow is available.
- Include a Loom video for every PR, including backend, refactor, and infrastructure changes. Keep it under 2–3 minutes, show before/after for bug fixes, and narrate key decisions. Put the link in Loom video.
- Assign a reviewer when ready. Do not mark a draft ready while required evidence or reviews remain incomplete.

## After merge

Delete the PR branch after a successful merge. Creating a draft does not authorize merging or deleting branches.

---
name: dg-pr-adherence-check
description: Review a PR or local diff for adherence to Discourse Graphs code standards and PR requirements, report concerns to the author, and return a Standards check checkbox. Use before handoff or requesting review, alongside scope-check.
---

# PR adherence check

Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.

## Resolve the evidence

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. For local work, compare with the merge base of the intended PR base and include staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked files. Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.
- Distinguish mandatory rules from preferences. Words such as “prefer” and “ideally,” the 200-line target, and the five-file guideline need judgment. Above 400 changed lines, excluding tests, check for the required explanation and review guide rather than rejecting the size alone.
- Explain concerns briefly to the PR author so they can address them; formal rule citations and evidence for each finding are not required. Do not invent exceptions, team approval, testing outcomes, or video contents. If a required document is unavailable or rules conflict without a clear applicable resolution, report the gap instead of guessing.
- Respect workflow timing: missing Loom or review evidence can be reported as outstanding before requesting review while a draft is being prepared. Do not call future post-merge steps violations on an open PR.
- Keep scope expansions in Scope check. Verification is optional. Standards check only records whether the check ran.

## Return the result

Return a copy-ready section:

```markdown
## Standards check

- [x] Ran `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata.
```

The checkbox means the review ran, not that all requirements passed. If the diff cannot be resolved or the review could not run, leave it unchecked and tell the author what blocked it. Separately make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them; do not require these details in the PR body. Rerun affected checks after changes to code, rules, or PR metadata.
SKILL.md

I'm leaning toward folding the node-type Content write into the schema Concept itself to preserve stored values without needing a CrossApp contract change, though I need to check how that interacts with the schema sync path.

Comparing the two schema conversion approaches, discourseNodeSchemaToLocalConcept and crossAppNodeSchemaToDbConcept end up producing nearly identical results—same name/label mapping, similar template and role handling, and comparable timestamp sourcing—so switching between them looks feasible but is really a separate piece of work for later.

For the suggestive-rules re-embedding, I need to think through whether writing concepts via the sync path risks wiping local_reference_content when a concept has no source, since PUT semantics mean omitted fields could overwrite existing data rather than leave it untouched.

For published node types, the re-embed shouldn't lose "full" content since upsert_content only touches the rows it's given, so other content stays intact.

Now I'm tracing through how isFirstChild gets handled across publish versus sync paths — publish uses title-only direct content while sync combines title and child text, and I need to check how this flows through the concept conversion logic.

I'm weighing a couple of contract changes to reconcile this: one option adds an optional variant field to the content type so crossAppNodeToDbContent can pick the right slot, but that breaks the name derivation since it currently just uses the direct content value, which would then wrongly include the child text. The other option is introducing a separate optional content key specifically for the combined title-and-description case, keeping name derivation untouched.

I'm also realizing this second approach would incidentally fix ENG-2426's stale-data issue as a side effect, since sync would start writing fresh direct rows just like publish does — which feels like scope creep, but may actually be justified since both paths should store identical values through the same converter.

Though wait, under this option sync's direct slot would actually hold direct_and_description, not direct — meaning sync and publish are writing different variants for the same node, so they wouldn't truly match. I also need to think about which variant keeps the embedding for isFirstChild nodes — currently it's on direct_and_description, and I'm checking whether match functions like the one in embedding.sql filter by variant, though that may not matter much here. There's also a third option worth considering: dropping direct_and_description entirely and having sync just write direct = title instead.

But that contradicts his own later name-derivation change to use the title, unless the naming logic gets updated to only use the direct value when the variant is direct. I'll present both options with that history, leaning toward Option 2 since it keeps direct as the title matching publish while giving description its own slot, and note it incidentally satisfies what ENG-2426 wants for published isFirstChild nodes even though that ticket was marked out of scope.

Now I'm also checking how author/created metadata flows through sync today—getNodeExtraData queries per node, and for page nodes the row author matches the page creator, but for isFirstChild nodes the child block's creator could differ from the page creator returned by getNodeExtraData, which matters for how concept authorship would change.

I could add the page creator into the isFirstChild query, but that touches another existing query, so I'll just flag it as a minor detail in the proposal with a default: accept that the concept author becomes the first child's creator unless we change the query. I'm realizing this creates a flip-flop — publish writes page creator as author while sync would write child creator for the same concept, which is a subtle inconsistency worth noting but not blocking.

That level of detail belongs in the PR description rather than the proposal itself — I should keep the proposal focused on the split plus the 2-3 decisions that actually need sid's input, with minor defaults mentioned briefly. THE PROBLEM
Sync has to write every node through the publish converter, `crossAppNodeToDbConcept`. Two things sync writes today don't fit it:
1. Nodes whose type uses a first-child description. Sync writes a `direct_and_description` Content ("page title + first child text"), and that Content carries the embedding. CrossAppNode only has `direct` and `full`, and the converter takes the Concept's name from `direct`. ENG-2128 (Marc-Antoine, after PR #1333) made these Concepts' name the page title, which is also what publish writes.
2. Node-type Content (`upsertNodeSchemaToContent`). Publish writes none.

PRs (stacked on ENG-2061)
1. packages/database: the CrossApp contract can carry the description Content, and `crossAppNodeToDbConcept` writes it. About 10 lines plus tests. PR_GUIDELINES asks for foundational type changes first.
2. apps/roam: sync writes each node instance and shared node in one `upsert_concepts` call: direct Content (plus the description and embedding where they apply) and full markdown for shared nodes, converted through `CrossAppNode` and `crossAppNodeToDbConcept`. The asset stage runs after the Concept upsert. Removes the `upsertNodes` and full-content `upsert_content` writes, and updates fileReferenceHarness.ts and syncSharedNodeAssets.test.ts. Estimated 250-300 lines excluding tests.
3. apps/roam: the remaining Content-only writes. Node-type Content goes into the schema Concept, the suggestive-rules re-embed uses PR 2's path, and the `upsert_content` writers are deleted, including an unused duplicate `upsertNodesToSupabaseAsContentWithEmbeddings` in upsertNodesAsContentWithEmbeddings.ts. This meets the Done When.

DECISIONS FOR SID
1. Description Content shape.
   A (recommended): add an optional `content.directAndDescription`, and `direct` stays the page title. Concept names don't change and match publish. Sync then also writes a plain `direct` Content for these nodes, which is ENG-2426's fix. ENG-2426 would close with PR 2, for unpublished nodes too.
   B (#1333): a `variant` field, with the description held in `direct`. ENG-2426 stays separate, but the converter would rename these Concepts to "title + description". That undoes ENG-2128 and disagrees with publish.
2. Node-type Content.
   A (recommended): keep writing it, embedded in the schema Concept (the existing schema converter plus `contents_inline`; moving schemas onto CrossApp stays in ENG-2165).
   B: stop writing it. Publish writes none, and the only code I found that reads these rows is cleanup's delete.
3. PR_GUIDELINES says one PR per Linear ticket. Three PRs need sub-tickets or an exception. I won't write to Linear unless sid asks.

DEFAULTS UNLESS SID OBJECTS
- 50 Concepts per call. A node is about 33 KB, almost all of it the embedding, so bytes per node are the same as today's 200-row `upsert_content` batches (6.7 MB). The reason for 50 is the database work per call: Concept, Content, Document and embedding together, which risks the statement timeout.
- Embeddings only for changed nodes. `upsert_content` writes an embedding only when one is sent, so a re-sent Content keeps its stored one.
- The full-content path adds the Source slot. Otherwise re-upserting a shared node's Concept would wipe its Source, because `upsert_concepts` replaces `reference_content`.
- First-child nodes keep the page creator as the Concept's author, as today and as publish does. The description Content keeps the child block's creator. This needs the page creator added to the first-child query.
- Drop `v_creator_id`: `upsert_content` doesn't read it.
- Telemetry: the `upsertNodes` and `upsertFullContent` phases fold into `convertConcepts`.

Out of scope, noting only: sync's `last_modified` uses `:edit/time`, while publish uses max(`:edit/time`, `:page/edit-time`). That difference already exists.

Git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` start with **no `node_modules`** — checks fail with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: @repo/eslint-config` because this is a pnpm workspace and `@repo/*` packages live in per-package `node_modules`.

**Why (updated 2026-07-10, ENG-2019):** Symlinks resolve `@repo/*` workspace packages to the MAIN repo's checkout. That's only correct when the worktree branch leaves `packages/*` untouched. If the branch adds/changes anything in `packages/*`, tsc/eslint see the stale main-repo copy; and MIXED states (some dirs symlinked, some real from a filtered install) are worst of all — one mix broke Roam's global types, another broke Obsidian's React 18/19 peer resolution.

**How to apply:**
- Branch touches only `apps/*` code: symlink root + per-package `node_modules` from the main repo (fast, gitignored, never committed).
- Branch touches `packages/*`: run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at the worktree root instead (shared pnpm store, ~5–45s). If a mixed symlink/real state exists, remove the symlinks and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --force` to rebuild the virtual store cleanly.
- Never run `--no-frozen-lockfile` casually: it re-resolves unrelated packages (an @types/node dedup cascaded into React type mixing that broke Obsidian tsc, would have been red CI). To add one dep, hand-add the importer entry to pnpm-lock.yaml reusing an existing catalog resolution (PR #1216 did it in 3 lines), then frozen install.

**Root `pnpm ci:validate` in a symlinked worktree (2026-09-02, ENG-2141):** symlink EVERY workspace that has a package.json, not just the ones you touch. `apps/tldraw-sync-worker/node_modules` was missing and turbo failed fast on its `check-types`, skipping every other task. Separately, the main checkout's virtual-store hoist `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/@types/react` was a July link to React 18 types while packages/ui needs 19, so `@repo/ui check-types` failed locally even though `.pnpm/lock.yaml` matched the lockfile and CI at the same commit was green. That is a main-checkout environment problem (a fresh frozen install there), not something to fix from a worktree. Fallback proof when it bites: `pnpm exec turbo run test:unit` at the worktree root plus per-app `tsc`, and cite the green CI run at the base SHA.

**Husky rewrites the shared hooks path (2026-09-25):** `pnpm install` in a worktree runs the root `prepare` script (`husky`), which sets the repo-wide `core.hooksPath` to relative `.husky/_`. The main checkout's value is absolute `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/.husky/_` (the Entire hook wrappers live there). After any worktree install, check `git config core.hooksPath` and restore the absolute value if it changed.

See [[feedback_stay_in_worktree]], [[feedback_rename_worktree_branch_before_push]], [[feedback_fix_relocated_lint_warnings]].

ENG-2061 is done and committed locally (not pushed). Before I write any ENG-1824 code, I need your OK on the split and three decisions below. Both reports went to `discourse-graph-92`.

## ENG-2061: committed locally

Branch `eng-2061-refactor-roamfullcontentnode-to-use-crossappnode-contract`, commit `b447ec86`, on origin/main `67e93a0d`, in worktree `.claude/worktrees/eng-2061`.

- `RoamFullContentNode` is gone. `fullContentNodeToCrossApp` now takes the shared `RoamDiscourseNodeData` row, as PR #1333 did, and gets the format from the node's type.
- On `RoamDiscourseNodeData`, the times are now typed `number` and `author_name` is optional. These are type changes only; nothing behaves differently.
- Following your 2026-10-22 decision, the full-content query still returns rows, not `CrossAppNode`. The conversion stays in the `upsertFullContent` phase, so no code moved. `convertRoamNodeToFullContent.ts` stays; only the type left it.
- eslint, prettier, tsc and `pnpm ci:validate` (712 Roam tests) all pass, with one exception: eslint reports 2 warnings in `getAllDiscourseNodesSince.ts` (lines 17 and 152). They were already there, and the diff doesn't touch those lines, so CI won't flag them.
- After you say push, these are still to do: Loom, `/pre-pr-review`, scope-check.

## ENG-1824: proposed 3 PRs, stacked on ENG-2061

1. **packages/database:** the CrossApp contract gains a way to carry the description Content (see decision 1). About 10 lines plus tests.
2. **apps/roam sync:** each node goes to the database in one `upsert_concepts` call, converted through `CrossAppNode` with the publish converter. That covers direct Content, the embedding, and full markdown for shared nodes. The asset upload runs after the Concept write. About 250–300 lines, not counting tests.
3. **apps/roam, the remaining Content-only writes:** node-type Content, the suggestive-rules re-embed, and an unused duplicate `upsert_content` writer. After this PR, no `upsert_content` call is left, which meets the Done When.

## Decisions I need from you

1. **How to store the description of nodes whose text lives in a first child block.** Today sync writes these as a `direct_and_description` Content, and that Content carries the embedding. The CrossApp contract only has `direct` and `full`, and the publish converter names the Concept after `direct`.
   - **A (recommended):** add an optional `content.directAndDescription`, and keep `direct` as the page title. Concept names stay as they are and match publish. Sync would also start writing a plain `direct` Content for these nodes, which is ENG-2426's fix. So ENG-2426 would close with PR 2, and the fix would cover unpublished nodes too.
   - **B (PR #1333's way):** put the description in `direct` with a `variant` field. ENG-2426 stays separate, but these Concepts get renamed to "title + description". That undoes ENG-2128 and no longer matches publish.
2. **Node-type Content.**
   - **A (recommended):** keep writing it, but inside the schema Concept.
   - **B:** stop writing it. Publish never writes it, and the only code I found touching it is cleanup's delete.
3. **PR_GUIDELINES says one PR per ticket.** Three PRs would need sub-tickets or an exception. I won't touch Linear unless you ask.

## What I'll do unless you object

- **Batch size 50:** that's 50 Concepts per call, as PR #1333 used. Each node is about 33 KB, almost all of it the embedding. That's the same bytes per node as today's 200-row `upsert_content` batches (6.7 MB). The reason for 50 is that each call now writes the Concept, its Content, Document and embedding at once, which risks the database statement timeout.
- **Source slot on shared nodes:** a shared node re-sent only for its full content keeps its Source. Otherwise `upsert_concepts` would wipe it.
- **Author of first-child nodes:** the Concept's author stays the page creator. This matches today and publish, and needs one extra field in that query.

I also updated the node_modules memory. The main checkout is on an older `main` whose `packages/*` differ from origin/main, so symlinking would have type-checked against stale code; I ran a frozen install in the worktree instead and restored `core.hooksPath`.

content.content:
=== feedback_pr_workflow_skills

On 2026-08-31 sid superseded the per-PR michael trio (/think-like-michael, /review-like-michael, /save-from-myself) because /pre-pr-review covers what they caught. The trio's command files still exist in ~/.claude/commands but are no longer part of the standing workflow; only invoke them if sid explicitly asks.

**Why:** the trio and /pre-pr-review overlapped heavily (all simulate the human review), and the team's new PR template (ENG-2206) added its own gates (scope-check section, delegated-review checkbox — satisfied by /pre-pr-review as the "other full-review workflow").

**How to apply, in order per PR:**
1. During implementation: `roam-global-tailwind` when touching Roam UI styling.
2. After push: `/pre-pr-review` as an independent Opus pass (see [[feedback_independent_pre_pr_review]]); rerun after follow-up pushes.
3. PR assembly: `scope-check` against the ticket's Done When; paste its `## Scope check` section into the PR body, which starts from `.github/pull_request_template.md` (see [[feedback-no-claude-footer-simple-prs]]).
4. `pr-video` only when the PR has no demo for the template's Loom section.
5. All team-facing prose uses `dg-engineering-writing-style`; tickets use `dg-create-engineering-ticket` (see [[feedback-use-dg-ticket-skills]]).
6. `ask-as-sid` is NOT used on the discourse-graph project.

Curt directives ("minimal commit push") still skip the per-PR skills, per [[feedback_minimal_means_skip_skills]].
=== feedback_independent_pre_pr_review

When sid says "use the pre-pr-review skill before PR", run `/home/sid/.claude/commands/pre-pr-review.md` as its own read-only pass (a fresh Opus agent per PR, against `gh pr diff N` plus the worktree) after implementation is done, and again after any follow-up commit. The implementing agent saying "I reviewed it" is not the review.

**Why:** On 2026-08-23 sid asked "for each of the pr you did .. did you do the pre-pr-review" for #1330/#1331/#1332; only self-reviews had run. Independent passes then found real defects the implementers missed: a producer key (`author_uid` vs `author_local_id`) that would have blanked `author_id` across the published corpus, a stale legacy-store cache after type creation, and a lossy `{Source}` decoration. See [[project-review-system-v2]].

**How to apply:** Launch the reviewers once the branch is pushed; adjudicate findings yourself (fix in-scope, defer with a note, never rubber-stamp); re-run after fix commits; report per PR what was fixed vs deferred. Don't create Linear tickets for deferrals on sid's behalf — list them for sid to file.

**Re-review mode (added 2026-09-01):** the skill file itself (`/home/sid/.claude/commands/pre-pr-review.md`, "Re-review mode (follow-up pushes)") defines DIFFERENT steps for follow-up pushes: delta only (`git diff <last-reviewed-sha>...HEAD`), findings-closure first (fixed/not-fixed/deferred per prior finding and reviewer/bot comment), steps 1–3 on the delta, shrunk step 4, escape hatch if the follow-up adds new surface. When launching the reviewer agent for a follow-up push, don't dictate scope in the launcher prompt (that's what went wrong on ENG-2088, 2026-09-01: the launcher hard-coded full-diff during a re-review) — pass the facts (last-reviewed SHA, what the push answers) and let the reviewer make the mode call via the skill's Mode gate. Per sid (same day): mode choice stays a judgment call, not a black/white rule — a follow-up push can genuinely warrant a full pass (new surface, moved base, doubtful prior coverage), and the reviewer should say which mode it chose and why.
=== feedback_no_extra_usage

Don't push the account into paid extra usage. The homeworld account has extra usage enabled, so once the 5-hour limit is used up, further work bills at API rates.

**Why:** on 2026-10-02 sid saw API pricing being charged. The cause was a long session plus five Opus research subagents, one of which used about 620k tokens. His words: "my api pricing is being used i don't want that to happen".

**How to apply:** keep research inline or use small targeted reads; launch subagents sparingly and never several Opus ones in parallel for gathering. This narrows [[feedback_delegate_gathering_to_opus]] whenever usage is a concern. If the session looks close to the limit, stop, write a handoff and say so.

**It happened again, 2026-10-08:** on the tutorial video series I had up to six max-effort Fable and Opus agents running at once: three part builders, two script reviews, a truth pass. Over the session, finished subagents used about 2M tokens; one truth pass alone used 465k. sid hit 88% of his weekly and 5-hour limits and wrote "i am getting scared … start using api prices … how much is pending??". I stopped all five running agents and wrote a handoff. Even when sid explicitly asks for max-effort thinking partners ([[feedback-creative-thinking-partners]]), run at most two agents at a time. Say what each will roughly cost before launching it. Never start build-phase fan-out without asking first.
=== feedback_minimal_means_skip_skills

When the user says "minimal commit push", "just commit", "ship it", or other curt commit directives, **skip** the mandatory 3-skill review pass ([[mandatory-rules]]: think-like-michael / review-like-michael / save-from-myself). They've already evaluated the diff and want to move.

**Why:** During ENG-1765, after I ran think-like-michael (which surfaced concerns the user implicitly chose not to act on), the user said "ok add, minimal commit push". I invoked review-like-michael per the standing rule and they rejected the tool use, then re-typed "add minimal commit push" to make the directive clearer. The standing rule says "don't skip skills even if user doesn't ask," but an explicit curt "minimal" overrides that — it's a deliberate scope signal, not an oversight.

**How to apply:**
- Lint + prettier + tsc checks: still run (those are fast and catch real breaks).
- Skill passes: skip when user explicitly says "minimal" / "just commit" / similar.
- If a skill already ran in this turn and surfaced concerns the user moved past, don't re-run others — they've seen the lens.
- Still respect other MEMORY rules (no Co-Authored-By, HEREDOC commit message, read diff before composing).
=== feedback_decide_dont_poll

On 2026-10-08 I stopped background agents because sid said he was scared of API overage. He then asked "but why stop?? what we gonna do now?????? how and when the videos will be made????". I answered with a two-question AskUserQuestion (continue or wait; which import flow) and he rejected it outright, then pasted the meeting transcript and expected me to work out the rest.

**Why:** he wants momentum and a straight plan. A menu, when I can reasonably decide, reads as handing the work back to him. This is the same pattern as the rejected three-option menu in [[feedback-blind-fresh-take]].

**How to apply:** state the decision, a one-line reason, and the next concrete action, then do it. For a real ambiguity, pick the most defensible reading, say it in one line, and offer to switch ("if X meant Y, tell me"). Keep usage lean per [[feedback-no-extra-usage]], but don't stop work without saying exactly how it resumes.
=== feedback_narrate_long_work

During long work, post a plain one- or two-line status every few tool calls: what I found, what I'm changing, what's next. End each phase with a short summary before starting the next.

**Why:** On 2026-10-08, fixing the proof runner's Flag box and case list, I read code and wrote tests for about 100 tool calls with almost no text in between. System nudges ("say what you're doing") got a few words each, then more silent calls. sid interrupted: "wtf is going on???". He wanted what was found, what was changed, what was verified and what wasn't. A clear status fixed it ("ok anything else?").

**How to apply:** Lead with the finding in plain words (the cause, the change, the proof), not a tour of files. Say what was verified and how (headless test, not real Roam). Name what's still open. This sits beside [[feedback_do_the_work]]: do the work, but keep him able to see where it is. Don't hand him a menu; state the plan and act ([[feedback-decide-dont-poll]]).
=== feedback_build_on_done_locally

On the Roam↔Obsidian push-pull project, the gate for building on a blocking ticket is **done-locally** — its code committed in its branch/worktree — **not** Linear "closed" or PR-merged. sid corrected this explicitly: "lets not say closed ... check roam logs if some agent has claimed they have finished work locally ... from there we can build on top."

**Why:** the project runs parallel agents on stacked branches; tickets are committed locally and stacked while their bases stay unmerged (e.g., ENG-1848 and ENG-1849 both stacked on the unmerged ENG-1847 branch). Gating on merge/closed would stall the whole stack.

**How to apply:** when your issue is blocked-by another, check the Roam Agent logs / Human Handoff (and `git worktree list`) for a "session complete — committed locally" claim on the blocker. If present, create your worktree branched off that blocker's branch tip and build on it; verify the commit exists (`git log`) before stacking. Only the **runtime** code you depend on must be present — a fixture-only blocker may not need stacking.
